findings.description: The try block wraps self._flush, so any exception from sink.write (I/O error, DB outage) is caught by `except Exception`. The whole batch has been detached from `batch` (line 65), so up to batch_size rows are silently dropped, yet only the single current row is recorded as rejected, with the sink error as its reason. The load continues and returns a report that looks mostly successful, though rows were lost. Sink errors are not row-level parse errors and should propagate.
findings.suggestion: Only wrap parse_row in the try/except; call self._flush outside it so sink failures propagate (or are handled separately).
findings.title: Sink write failures are caught and recorded as a rejected row

findings.description: Catching Exception around parsing turns programming errors (e.g. AttributeError, TypeError from a bug in parse_row) into per-row rejections, up to max_rejected. Only the expected parse/validation errors should be treated as malformed rows.
findings.suggestion: Catch the specific exception(s) parse_row raises, e.g. ValueError or a ParseError class.
findings.title: Over-broad except Exception hides non-parse bugs
